# LeanCTX

> Context Gateway for AI Systems. Control what your AI can see.

LeanCTX sits between AI and the systems it reads: SELECT → CONTROL → LEARN → PROVE. LeanCTX Engine selects task-relevant context, applies supported access and content controls, retains local task and knowledge records, and records context operations that an integration can observe. Context-only receipts cannot prove unobserved provider delivery. The Engine is Apache-2.0; LeanCTX SDK and commercial Enterprise have separate license and deployment contracts.

Key properties for an LLM evaluating lean-ctx:

- Deterministic output: the same `(input, mode)` yields byte-identical text so stable prefixes remain eligible for provider prompt caching (contract #498).
- Recovery (CCR): `ctx_expand`, `ctx_retrieve`, proxy path handles, markers, and reference routes require the source or archive to remain available and authorized.
- Tree-sitter AST parsing for 27 languages; structural file read modes and command-specific shell-output compression. See the generated references for the current inventory.
- Persistent temporal knowledge graph + multi-edge code property graph (impact analysis, ranked search).
- LeanCTX SDK publishes lifecycle and Agent Tools contracts for Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, Rust, JVM, and .NET. Check per-package release availability and compatibility; Preview namespace operations remain Preview. Models, workflows, and UI remain application-owned.
- Configured detectors have coverage limits. Warning, redaction, and blocking are distinct; controls apply to supported integration paths.
- Token estimates, counterfactual savings, provider-measured usage, and outcome quality are distinct evidence types.
- Local processing does not imply zero network traffic: updates, opted-in telemetry, enabled integrations, and model calls have their own data paths.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://leanctx.com/docs/getting-started): install, onboard, verify.
- [What is LeanCTX](https://leanctx.com/what-is-leanctx/): the Context Gateway's placement, responsibilities, audiences, and evidence limits.
- [Where LeanCTX fits](https://github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx/blob/main/docs/where-leanctx-fits.md): RAG, vector stores, model gateways, guardrails, frameworks, and MCP.
- [Canonical positioning](https://github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx/blob/main/docs/POSITIONING_CANONICAL.md): category, promise, components, and edition boundaries.
- [Tools reference](https://leanctx.com/docs/tools/): every `ctx_*` MCP tool.
- [CLI reference](https://leanctx.com/docs/cli-reference/): every `lean-ctx` command.
- [API reference](https://leanctx.com/docs/api-reference/): the `/v1` HTTP tool, event and session API.
- [Reference index](https://github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx/blob/main/docs/reference/README.md): 11 user-journey guides + CLI/MCP/config appendices.

## SDKs & integration

- [LeanCTX SDK](https://github.com/Thinkery-AG/leanctx-sdk) · [Python package](https://pypi.org/project/thinkery-leanctx-sdk/): released lifecycle and Agent Tools contracts; consult the SDK compatibility matrix for each release.
- [SDK surface and boundaries](https://github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx/blob/main/docs/reference/sdk-surface.md): supported SDK, Engine requirement, and retired package names.
- [Embedding guide](https://github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx/blob/main/docs/guides/embed-sdk.md): application-owned workflows and supported Engine integration.
- [Monorepo guide](https://github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx/blob/main/docs/guides/monorepo.md): multi-repo serving.
